svg.title: Thermal two-copy squeeze, closure projection, and geometry
svg.desc: A two-copy squeeze preserves a combined dual closure condition, while separate projection restores ordinary closure in each copy and leaves area free to fluctuate.
svg.text: Heating two copies separates combined closure from geometry
For the studied reference, a squeeze adds correlated quanta; separate singlet projection keeps both copies closed.
Before projection, ordinary closure can fail in each copy; its defect grows with the squeeze parameter.
Separately closed state and its readouts
Each copy is an ordinary singlet;
its area still fluctuates between sectors.
Area-one reference: projected mean area and
positive RS volume rise as T* increases.
The squeeze parameter labels a preparation; it does not prove Gibbs equilibrium for the excited projected state.
Results use one explicit, initially degenerate two-face reference.
